newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SEZ Real Estate to report lower '96 net.
newsitem.headline: SEZ Real Estate to report lower '96 net.

text.p: Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Real Estate and Properties (Group) Co Ltd estimated that its net profits for 1996 would be lower than the 1995 figures, a company spokesman said on Monday.

The firm has a number of empty property projects on its books, mainly high-priced office buildings in Shenzhen, Beijing and Shanghai, which resulted in lower earnings, he told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The spokesman declined to say how much the company expect its 1996 results would fall below the 1995 level.
Under Chinese accounting standards, the company had after-tax profits of 392.41 million yuan in 1995, compared with 448.97 million yuan in 1994.
It reported unaudited profits of 151.56 million yuan in the first half of 1996 against 150.92 million yuan in the same 1995 period.
The spokesman said demand for property remained rather weak throughout 1996 despite the two cuts in bank interest rates during the year, he said.
The lower interest rates led to a fall in the firm's finance-related costs but the impact on its earnings was quite limited, the official said but gave no further details.
It said the earnings growth came on the back of a 27.1 percent rise in its main operating income, which hit 591.40 million yuan versus 465.31 million yuan in the 1995 period.
